patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive personality change with disinhibition, compulsive eating, loss of empathy, and poor hygiene.
patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. K. is a 58-year-old right-handed White male brought in by his wife of 30 years for progressive personality and behavioral changes over the past 2 years. His wife reports that the change began subtly — he became less interested in conversation, more irritable, and started making inappropriate comments at family gatherings. Over the following year, the changes became unmistakable: he began making sexually explicit remarks to female neighbors, laughed at his granddaughter's injury, and showed complete indifference when their dog died. She describes him as having 'lost his soul.' He has developed compulsive behaviors: he insists on eating the same three meals daily, paces the living room for exactly 30 minutes every evening, and has begun hoarding items from grocery stores. His diet has changed dramatically — he craves sweets and high-calorie foods and has gained 18 pounds. His personal hygiene is severely degraded; his wife must physically guide him to shower.

Professionally, he retired from accounting 2 years ago after colleagues reported he was making errors in client accounts and had made inappropriate comments to staff. He shows no insight into his deficits and is not distressed. His wife has discovered he has been making online purchases totaling over $14,000, mostly buying things that he immediately forgets having ordered. His alcohol use has escalated from 1-2 beers occasionally to 6-8 beers nightly, which he denies entirely. He has never had psychiatric illness and there is no family history of dementia. Neurological review of systems is otherwise negative.

findings.finding: Severe hypometabolism, symmetric, involving prefrontal, orbitofrontal, and cingulate cortex

advanced_imaging.impression: Severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex metabolism preserved

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. Global SUVR 0.94, below positivity threshold

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 125 mmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 44 mg/dL. Glucose: 61 mg/dL (ratio 0.69). Abeta42: 798 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 231 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 38 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 2,104 pg/mL (elevated — consistent with neurodegeneration). 14-3-3 protein: negative.

Severely impaired — Faux Pas Test: 3/20; complete failure on perspective-taking and social inference tasks
Moderately impaired but predominantly retrieval-based (frontal) — free recall impaired, cued recall relatively better; CVLT-II: 15th percentile with cueing benefit
Intact naming; reduced verbal fluency consistent with frontal dysfunction
FrSBe: severe disinhibition (98th percentile), severe apathy (91st percentile), executive dysfunction (96th percentile); NPI-Q caregiver distress: 24/36

output.proposed: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (sertraline 100 mg/day) for behavioral symptoms in bvFTD
interactions: Metformin + sertraline: minimal interaction; monitor blood glucose as SSRIs can affect glycemic control

warnings: Metformin + sertraline: SSRIs may affect glycemic control; monitor blood glucose
Benzodiazepines: increased fall risk and potential paradoxical disinhibition in elderly patients
Antipsychotics: increased cerebrovascular event risk in dementia; use with caution and specialist oversight

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Older adult with cognitive decline; would expect posterior parietotemporal hypometabolism and positive amyloid biomarkers — case shows frontal-predominant atrophy and negative amyloid PET.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (late-onset mood / personality disorder, frontal alcoholism)
differential.key_features: Heavy alcohol escalation could mimic disinhibition; severe knife-blade frontal atrophy, frontal release signs, and utilisation behavior are organic findings inconsistent with a primary psychiatric diagnosis.

Recent alcohol escalation; pattern of frontal atrophy + posterior sparing is more severe and focal than typical alcohol-related changes; alcohol escalation itself is likely a symptom of frontal disinhibition.
Gait shuffling could suggest NPH but no urinary incontinence, no disproportionate ventriculomegaly, and atrophic pattern dominates.
No fasciculations, bulbar dysfunction, or limb weakness; EMG not yet pursued but no clinical motor neuron signs.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI with volumetric coronal T1 to assess frontal/anterior temporal atrophy and exclude alternative structural cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy in a lobar pattern with relative posterior sparing

optimal_actions.action: Order metabolic dementia panel (TSH, B12, CMP, RPR/HIV per risk) to exclude reversible mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No reversible metabolic or infectious cause of cognitive decline identified

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery characterising executive function, social cognition, language and memory
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-executive and social-cognition deficits with relative sparing of episodic memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for behavioural variant ftd diagnosis and management
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms Rascovsky 2011 criteria, FDG-PET evidence (Foster 2007), and management approach (Bang 2015)

tool_parameters.query: Behavioural variant FTD diagnosis and management

optimal_actions.action: Consult behavioral/cognitive neurology for syndromic diagnosis, biomarker interpretation, and longitudinal care plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Behavioral neurology confirms bvFTD syndrome, coordinates biomarkers and disclosure

optimal_actions.action: Order FDG-PET brain to characterise frontotemporal hypometabolism and distinguish bvFTD from AD
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bifrontal and/or anterior temporal hypometabolism with relative posterior sparing
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.action: Order FTD genetic panel (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT) given negative family history but to formally exclude C9orf72/GRN/MAPT given young age and severity
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identifies or excludes pathogenic C9orf72 / GRN / MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and cascade testing

optimal_actions.action: Consider amyloid PET to exclude AD biomarker positivity when FDG and MRI alone leave residual diagnostic uncertainty
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Negative amyloid PET supports non-AD (bvFTD) etiology
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.action: Consider symptomatic SSRI (e.g., sertraline) for disinhibition / compulsive behaviors and review drug interactions
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sertraline safe with current regimen; no contraindication; advise against AChE inhibitors

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

sequence_constraints.reason: Exclude structural cause of focal cognitive symptoms and screen for elevated ICP before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Address escalating alcohol use as a symptom of frontal disinhibition rather than the primary cause; coordinate medical and behavioural intervention.
Initiate driving safety assessment and remove access to large financial transactions until capacity is formally evaluated.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
Do not attribute the syndrome to alcohol alone: the structural and metabolic frontotemporal pattern is not explained by alcohol-related cognitive disorder.
key_reasoning_points: Five Rascovsky core features are present (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, perseverative/compulsive behavior, hyperorality) plus executive dysfunction on FAB and neuropsychological testing — comfortably meets ≥3 of 6.
Knife-blade gyral atrophy on coronal T1 with bifrontal and anterior temporal volume loss is highly characteristic of FTLD; preserved hippocampal volume and posterior cortex argue against AD.
Severe bifrontal hypometabolism on FDG-PET with preserved posterior cingulate metabolism is the classic FTD pattern (Foster 2007).
Negative amyloid PET and normal CSF Aβ42/p-tau effectively exclude underlying neurodegenerative pathology, securing the bvFTD diagnosis.
Mild bilateral upper-extremity rigidity and shuffling gait do not justify DaTscan — extrapyramidal features can occur in advanced bvFTD and the imaging pattern already explains the syndrome.

red_herrings.data_point: Escalation of alcohol intake from 1–2 to 6–8 beers nightly
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests primary alcohol-related cognitive disorder driving disinhibition.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Escalating alcohol use in this context is itself a manifestation of frontal disinhibition; the structural/metabolic frontotemporal pattern is not explained by alcohol.

red_herrings.data_point: Mild bilateral cogwheel upper-extremity rigidity and shuffling gait
red_herrings.intended_effect: Could prompt DaTscan for suspected parkinsonism.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild extrapyramidal features are common in advanced bvFTD and do not warrant DaTscan once the frontotemporal imaging pattern is established.

red_herrings.data_point: Glucose 112 mg/dL flagged as abnormal in BMP
red_herrings.intended_effect: Could be over-interpreted as metabolic contribution; agent might pursue additional metabolic workup.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild hyperglycaemia is consistent with the patient's known type 2 diabetes mellitus and does not explain frontotemporal degeneration.
